text:
The Trostead Compact spent twenty years defined by a fragile alliance with House Buldbei, a bond forged by three marriages in the first six years and broken by war in the ninth. The period began with the Compact holding Geirnpei Shafts, a site it had occupied in the second year, and ended with that same site lost to the Galweall League. Throughout the era, the Compact’s standing eroded from a position of strength to one where its authority had fallen to nothing, leading to the loss of Pellweagate and the eventual destruction of its grip on the region. Six people held the seat, passing the power five times through death, coup, and succession.

Faellwil Na ruled at the start, his reign ending when he was killed by Lald Neirntean in the fourth year. Neinos Del, the named heir, took the seat after rejecting the rival claim of Frernli Peimeath, who was cast out. Neinos Del died in the fifth year, and Neallseis Staend succeeded by right of birth. Neallseis Staend’s rule ended in the tenth year when Paepu Noth challenged him and won, taking the seat by coup and casting Neallseis Staend out. Paepu Noth ruled until he was killed by Lald Neirntean in the seventeenth year. Kesfound Thrael took the seat by right of birth, only to be killed by Lald Neirntean in the twentieth year. Vun Doultheam took the seat in the twentieth year and held it at the end of the period.

The Compact’s relationship with House Buldbei shifted from alliance to conflict. After declaring war on House Buldbei in the ninth year for Pei Delve, the Compact broke its alliance with them. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at Pei Delve in the ninth and tenth years, killing 23 and 18 men respectively. The Compact and House Buldbei made peace after two years of war. The Compact sent four raids, all carrying off plunder: two against Gaehollow and two against Themoor. It suffered ten raids, including those by the Galweall League and House Buldbei. The Galweall League declared war on the Compact in the nineteenth year over a long-standing grievance. The Compact defeated the Galweall League at Geirnpei Shafts in the nineteenth year, killing 19. In the twentieth year, the Galweall League and its allies defeated the Compact at Geirnpei Shafts, killing 16, and took the site. The two powers made peace after two years.

Internal stability collapsed as the Compact’s standing fell. Pellweagate rose against the Compact in the tenth year, when its standing had fallen to nothing, and broke away as the Rising of Pellweagate in the sixteenth year. Geirnpei Shafts rose against the Compact in the fifteenth year, also when its standing had fallen to nothing. Famine struck Geirnpei Shafts and Pellweagate for eight years, killing 209 people and causing 214 to flee. The Compact lost Pellweagate in the sixteenth year and Geirnpei Shafts in the twentieth year. Three people were cast out: Gall Brolllea for conspiracy, Frernli Peimeath for a losing claim, and Neallseis Staend for the losing side of a coup. The quarrel between the Compact and House Buldbei resulted in two battles.

The Rising of Pellweagate spent its twenty-two years in a state of collapse, defined by repeated failure and internal fracture. It began in year 16 when Veith Hei took the seat after Pellweagate broke from the Trostead Compact. The period was marked by four years of hunger that killed 173 people, six raids that were all beaten off, and a succession that shifted from one ruler to another. The power ended in year 37 not with a restoration, but with its destruction by the Galweall League, which had defeated it in battle and taken its land.

Veith Hei held the seat for sixteen years, during which the Rising suffered three famines and launched raids that failed against Trostead, Gaehollow, Geirnpei Shafts, Themoor, and Pei Delve. In year 32, Find Bound challenged Veith Hei openly for the seat, won, and cast him out. Find Bound’s rule was brief; he took the seat in year 32, but his house ended in year 37. During this time, three exiles returned to serve the Rising: Beasre Feanwoul and Find Bound in year 26, and Besveir Maleal in year 33. Find Bound married Draemo Grirn in year 27, binding the Rising to the Trostead Compact, and he won Beasre Feanwoul away from Veith Hei in year 30.

The final years saw the Rising drawn into war with the Galweall League. The League declared war in year 36 over a long-standing grievance, broke its alliance with the Rising, and defeated it at Pellweagate, where 136 died. The League took Pellweagate from the Rising in year 36, and the Rising was finished, its last four followers scattering. The Galweall League and the Rising made peace in year 37 after one year of war. The Rising had fought one battle, lost it, and lost its only place.

The period of House Buldbei’s existence in year 43 was defined by its abrupt termination. The house, which had operated under a succession by strongest, ended in that same year. Its collapse was not a gradual decline but a singular event that concluded its rule.

The end of House Buldbei coincided with a diplomatic shift in the region. In 43, the Galweall League and House Buldbei made peace. This agreement followed the collapse of House Buldbei, marking the final interaction between the two powers. The peace settlement served as the formal closure to the house’s presence.

The Galweall League’s decade was defined by a rapid succession of rulers and a collapse of internal stability. At the start of 42, the League held Micrag and stood in opposition to House Buldbei. The period opened with a coup by Keandtei Taegro, who took the seat from Lan Thraestun. This internal shift coincided with a war against House Buldbei, which the League won at Micrag, taking the settlement and ending House Buldbei’s existence. However, the League’s standing fell to nothing by the end of 42, allowing Pei Delve to rise against it. The period ended in 51 with Greimfourn Goul holding the seat, having killed Mound Sith in an open challenge.

The seat passed seven times between eight people, with an average tenure of 1.1 years. Five rulers were killed and two were cast out. Keandtei Taegro ruled for one year before being murdered by Del Monbirn. Veith Hei took the seat by election, setting aside the claim of Haeldkeind Nen, but was cast out after losing an open challenge to Nond Mea. Nond Mea’s rule ended when he was killed by Rusund Gilteil, who had challenged him openly. Rusund Gilteil was then murdered by Was Leithwon. Varnnael Wansen took the seat by election, setting aside Peansith Rae, but was killed by Rend Greall. Mound Sith took the seat by election after Wansen’s death.

Internal violence was the dominant feature of the period. Five people were murdered from within the League’s own ranks. Del Monbirn was cast out for conspiracy, as was Vaswei Grand. Was Leithwon was cast out for conspiracy after his murder of Rusund Gilteil. The League’s cohesion was further eroded by fifteen instances of people being courted away from its rulers, including multiple attempts to win Homraell Leill and Guthwaell Wound. Seven people were cast out in total: three for conspiracy, two for losing a claim, one for the losing side of a coup, and one for the losing side of an open challenge. The League fought one battle, which it won, and took one place, Micrag, but suffered no defeats in combat.

House Buldbei’s rule, governed by the strongest claim, ended in ruin after twenty years of escalating conflict with the Galweall League. The period began with the house’s standing already fallen to nothing, a condition that allowed Pei Delve to rise against it in 28. The house’s internal cohesion fractured early, as Beasre Feanwoul was cast out in 24 for an attempted murder on Lall Nealdgum, and later declared an outlaw for a conspiracy uncovered in 26. Lall Nealdgum remained the ruler until 34, when he was killed by Dreamwein Vous at Micrag. Hibrei Fou took the seat that same year by the strongest claim, followed by Thimseild Soldrind in 39 after Hibrei was murdered by Soldrind. Thimseild was cast out in 42 for an attempted murder, leaving the house without a holder as it was destroyed.

The Galweall League initiated two wars against House Buldbei, resulting in three battles that the house lost entirely. In 32, the League defeated Buldbei at Pei Delve, taking the site and killing 12. In 33, they defeated Buldbei at Micrag, killing 235. The war ended in 34 with peace between exhausted sides, but hostilities resumed in 42 over a long-standing grievance. In that final year, the League defeated Buldbei at Micrag again, killing 191 and taking the place. The house’s military efforts were equally unsuccessful; of six raids sent out, five were beaten off and one carried off plunder, while it suffered one raid on Micrag that took nothing.

Internal violence and external pressure eroded the house’s power. Two people were killed by their own, and three were cast out. Four exiles returned to take service, but one, Dreamwein Vous, was courted away to the Galweall League in 38. The house lost two places, Pei Delve in 32 and Micrag in 42. Hunger at Micrag in 26 and 27 killed 261 people and drove 262 away, while hunger at Pei Delve in 26 and 27 killed 3 and drove 20 away. The period ended in 42 with House Buldbei finished, landless, and its last follower scattered.

The Galweall League spent twenty years defined by internal instability and external warfare. Its leadership changed hands eight times, with nine individuals holding the seat in total. The period began with Threth Kruth ruling and ended with Lan Thraestun in possession. The seat passed through four castings out, three killings, and one natural death. The League fought four battles, winning all of them, and initiated three wars. It suffered thirteen raids, all of which were beaten off, and sent two raids that got through but took nothing.

Early in the period, the League faced famine at Themoor and Gaehollow in 23, killing 192 people. In 25, Dreamwein Vous married Veith Hei, binding the League to the Rising of Pellweagate. Threth Kruth remained in power until his death in 30. His rule ended when Del Monbirn had Tha Vu murdered at Trostead. Draemo Grirn then took the seat, setting aside the claim of Hibrei Fou, who was cast out. Thimseild Soldrind challenged Draemo Grirn openly in 31 but lost and was cast out. Besveir Maleal defeated Draemo Grirn in an open challenge in 32 and took the seat.

Besveir Maleal’s rule was short. Thimseild Soldrind challenged him and won, taking the seat by coup. Dreamwein Vous then challenged Thimseild Soldrind openly in 33 and won. Dreamwein Vous ruled until he was challenged by Thaham Geth in 36. Thaham Geth won the challenge and took the seat by coup. Dreamwein Vous was cast out. Thaham Geth was killed by Laelldou Nerum in 38 after Laelldou Nerum won an open challenge. Laelldou Nerum was killed by Lurntu Skondbea in 39 after Lurntu Skondbea won an open challenge. Lurntu Skondbea was killed by Lan Thraestun in 41 after Lan Thraestun won an open challenge.

The League’s external conflicts were intense. It declared war on the Trostead Compact in 29 over a long-standing grievance. The League defeated the Compact at Trostead, taking the settlement. The Compact was finished. The League declared war on House Buldbei in 32 for Pei Delve. The League defeated House Buldbei at Pei Delve and Micrag, taking Pei Delve. Peace was made after two years. The League declared war on the Rising of Pellweagate in 36. The League defeated the Rising at Pellweagate, taking the settlement. The Rising was finished. The quarrel between the League and House Buldbei persisted, resulting in two battles. The League sent two raids, one on Trostead in 22 and one on Micrag in 39, both taking nothing. It suffered thirteen raids, all beaten off. Six of its own people were murdered from within. Ten people were cast out. Two exiles returned. Two people were declared outlaw.

The Trostead Compact’s nine-year existence ended in ruin, its power dismantled by internal betrayal and external conquest. The period began with the Compact’s raid on Geirnpei Shafts beaten off in 22, a failure mirrored later that year when the Galweall League raided Trostead, killing 25 but taking nothing. The Compact’s stability was fragile from the start, relying on a succession by primogeniture that could not withstand the violence within its own ranks.

Vun Doultheam, who had held the seat since 20, was murdered at Trostead in 25 by Tha Vu. Besveir Maleal took the seat by right of birth immediately after, but his rule was short-lived. In 27, Del Monbirn challenged Besveir Maleal openly, won, and took the seat. Besveir Maleal was cast out as the losing side of that challenge. Tha Vu’s conspiracy against Del Monbirn was uncovered after three years, and Tha Vu was cast out for that conspiracy. The seat passed from one person to another two times inside this period, with one ruler killed, one cast out, and one whose house ended.

The Compact’s external relations deteriorated rapidly. It sent two raids, both beaten off: one on Geirnpei Shafts in 22 and one on Gaehollow in 28. In 28, Keandtei Taegro married Thimseild Soldrind, binding the Compact to the Galweall League. This alliance did not last. In 29, the Galweall League declared war on the Compact over a long-standing grievance and broke its alliance. The Galweall League and its allies defeated the Compact at Trostead, with 167 dead, and took the settlement. The Compact was finished, landless, its last 7 followers scattering. The Galweall League and the Compact made peace in 30 after one year of war.

The Galweall League’s twenty-year span from 2 to 21 was defined by a cycle of raiding, assassination, and shifting alliances with the Trostead Compact. The period opened with a marriage between Paernso Feand and Trurnur Draeltheas, binding the League to House Buldbei, and closed with a similar union between Sealfeis Vearn and Beasre Feanwoul, reinforcing that same tie. Throughout the years, the League engaged in five raids against the Compact, three of which carried off plunder, one was beaten off, and one returned empty-handed. The Compact retaliated with four raids of its own, all successful in taking grain and lives from League settlements.

Internal stability was fragile, marked by the return of five exiles who took service with the League, yet undermined by lethal purges. Lald Neirntean, who held the seat from before year 2, ordered the murders of Faellwil Na, Paepu Noth, and Kesfound Thrael at Trostead and Themoor. His rule ended in year 21 when Paernso Feand had him killed at Themoor, an act of retribution for a defeat suffered in year 19. Threth Kruth took the seat by election following Neirntean’s death, remaining in power as the period closed.

The military conflict between the League and the Trostead Compact escalated into a declared war in year 19. The Compact defeated the League at Geirnpei Shafts in year 19, killing 19 men. The League reversed this outcome in year 20, defeating the Compact at the same site with 16 dead and taking Geirnpei Shafts from them. After two years of war, both sides made peace in year 21, exhausted by the fighting. The quarrel between the two powers had resulted in two battles, one loss and one win for the League, ending with the League holding the territory it had captured.

The period from 3 to 22 was defined by internal violence and a persistent, two-year war with the Trostead Compact. House Buldbei’s rule was unstable, with the seat passing between five people in twenty years. The house began with Skengaer Tharsoull, who was killed in 7, and ended with Lall Nealdgum, who held the seat at the close of the period. The conflict with the Trostead Compact began in 9 and lasted for two years, resulting in two battles at Pei Delve, both won by House Buldbei.

Internal instability was driven by assassinations and coups. Skengaer Tharsoull was killed by Trurnur Draeltheas in 7. Threth Kruth took the seat by the strongest claim in 8, but Trurnur Draeltheas challenged and won, taking the seat by coup in the same year. Trurnur Draeltheas was murdered by Lall Nealdgum in 9. Kesfound Thrael took the seat by the strongest claim in 9, but Lall Nealdgum challenged and won, taking the seat by coup in 12. Two people were cast out, both as the losing side of a coup. One person, Threth Kruth, was declared outlaw after a conspiracy was uncovered.

The war with the Trostead Compact began in 9 when the Compact declared war for Pei Delve and broke its alliance with House Buldbei. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at Pei Delve in 9, killing 23, and again in 10, killing 18. Peace was made in 11 after two years of war. House Buldbei sent four raids during this period. One raid on Trostead in 4 was beaten off. Two raids, on Pellweagate in 10 and Geirnpei Shafts in 11, got through but took nothing. One raid on Trostead in 20 carried off 32 grain and killed 26.

Pei Delve suffered from hunger for four years, killing 41 people and causing 60 to flee. In 9, Pei Delve rose against House Buldbei, whose standing had fallen to nothing. Seven people were courted away from the ruler during this period. The quarrel between House Buldbei and the Trostead Compact resulted in two battles.

Greimfourn Goul took the seat of the Galweall League in 51 by defeating Mound Sith in an open challenge. The previous ruler, Mound Sith, was killed by Goul at Themoor later that same year.

The Galweall League spent 140 silver to buy back goodwill.

Goul’s rule ended in 51.

The Trostead Compact declared war on House Buldbei in year 9, seeking control of Pei Delve. House Buldbei and its allies defeated the Compact at that site later the same year, with 23 dead. The Compact suffered another defeat at Pei Delve in year 10, where 18 died.

The conflict lasted two years. In year 11, the Trostead Compact and House Buldbei made peace, both sides exhausted.

The Galweall League declared war on the Trostead Compact in 19, citing a long-standing grievance. The Trostead Compact defeated the Galweall League at Geirnpei Shafts in the same year, with 19 dead. In 20, Lald Neirntean had Kesfound Thrael murdered at Themoor. Later that year, the Galweall League and its allies defeated the Trostead Compact at Geirnpei Shafts, with 16 dead. The Galweall League took Geirnpei Shafts from the Trostead Compact in 20.

The war ended in 21 when the Galweall League and the Trostead Compact made peace after 2 years, both sides exhausted.
